item.title: Bottas urged to quit F1 for good: 'Get on your bike and enjoy your life'
item.description: Ralf Schumacher believes Cadillac should replace Valtteri Bottas with Esteban Ocon , arguing that the Frenchman would be a better option for the American team. The former F1 driver made his position clear while discussing Cadillac's first season in the championship, although he stressed that his criticism of Bottas was strictly related to his performances on track. Bottas returned to Formula 1 with Cadillac in 2026 after spending a year without a race seat, joining fellow comeback driver Sergio Perez. Both arrived with considerable experience, but the American outfit has struggled to compete with the established teams during its debut campaign. Schumacher wants Cadillac to replace Bottas with Ocon Speaking on the Backstage Boxengasse podcast, Schumacher identified Haas driver Esteban Ocon as the man he would like to see Cadillac bring into its line-up: "I would definitely take Ocon immediately." The German was careful to distinguish his opinion of Bottas as a driver from his feelings towards him personally. He described the Finn as "totally likeable" and stressed that his comments should "please not be taken personally". Nevertheless, Schumacher believes Cadillac would be better served by making a change. "But from a purely sporting point of view," he explained, before suggesting that Bottas should "get on your bike and enjoy your life". Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures The remark also brought to mind Bottas's recent cycling trip from Malaysia to Singapore, which he documented on social media. Cycling has become a major part of the Finn's life away from Formula 1, and Schumacher's comments suggested that he might be better off concentrating on his interests outside racing. Ocon, meanwhile, is currently racing for Haas but does not have a seat confirmed for the 2027 season. The Frenchman continued competing in Formula 1 throughout 2025, unlike Bottas, who spent the year on the sidelines before returning with Cadillac. How Bottas and Perez have performed at Cadillac in 2026 Cadillac opted for experience when selecting its first Formula 1 driver pairing. Bottas arrived with ten Grand Prix victories from his time at Mercedes, while Perez brought six wins and several seasons of experience alongside Max Verstappen at Red Bull. However, neither driver has managed to score a point for the team so far in 2026. Cadillac has spent much of its debut campaign towards the back of the field, with both drivers regularly fighting outside the top ten. Bottas recorded one of the team's strongest results with 13th place at the Chinese Grand Prix, although his season has also been disrupted by retirements and reliability problems. Perez has similarly struggled to break into the points. item.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Thursday, October 22
item.description: Mateus Fernandes of Tottenham Hotspur warms up before the Premier League match between Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford in Manchester, United Kingdom, on October 10, 2026. (Photo by Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Good morning! In recent weeks we’ve discussed new species of cats and penguins. Today it’s a plant. But this one is football related. It appears scientists have discovered a new species of plant in the Peruvian Andes. This has some blue flowers, and those who discovered it wanted to name it “salvia messii” after Lionel Messi, who plays alongside Marcos Senesi for the Argentinian national football team. A newly discovered plant in Peru has been named after Lionel Messi, called Salvia messi. item.title: NFL sends blunt message to Mike Vrabel with hefty fine over officials incident
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has reportedly been fined $250,000 by the NFL for his conduct towards officials, with two other head coaches receiving the same punishment. According to Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni and New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn have also been hit with the hefty penalties. The fines follow growing scrutiny of interactions between coaches and officials, with the league seemingly determined to make its expectations clear. Mike Vrabel’s $250,000 fine could be overturned with good behaviour Breer described the punishments as a clear statement from the NFL but suggested there could be a way for the three coaches to avoid paying. He wrote: “That, of course, is a pretty stiff penalty and a clear statement. I’ve also heard that the fines are in abeyance, meaning they’d be on hold, and could be repealed with good behavior.” Vrabel’s fine stems from a confrontation with an official during Week 4. The Patriots coach addressed the incident after the game and insisted his comments were not derogatory. “I told him it was a terrible — I’m not going to say effing — call. I’ve said that 87 times since I’ve been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You’d have to ask him,” Vrabel said. “I think he was a little sensitive.” The size of the reported fine has raised eyebrows, particularly because the NFL has not publicly detailed the specific behaviour that prompted the punishment. Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio described the penalties as “borderline cartoonish”, arguing that the league had not clearly explained what the coaches had done to warrant such significant fines. There is also uncertainty surrounding what the NFL would consider good behaviour and whether the three coaches can successfully appeal. For New England, the figure is particularly striking given that the franchise received a $250,000 fine during the Spygate scandal, alongside the forfeiture of a first-round draft pick. Vrabel must now turn his attention to the Patriots’ next challenge, with the team preparing to visit the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football. The reported punishment also sends a warning to other head coaches, although clearer guidance from the NFL may be needed if the league expects them to avoid similar sanctions. Read more: Travis Kelce shares why people keep thanking him on the street since he started dating Taylor Swift ‘Flying all over the place’ – Travis Kelce says Chiefs linebacker ‘doesn’t get enough credit’ Kurt Warner shares Fernando Mendoza verdict after what he’s seen from Kirk Cousins

item.title: Clippers dethrone the Sacramento Kings in regular-season opener
item.description: Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) makes a deep three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES - The Los Angeles Clippers entered tonight’s regular-season opener with a lot of questions to be answered amid all the off-season turmoil and an injury list that piled on throughout the offseason. Yet, the Clippers answered the call tonight with a resounding 121-96 victory over the Sacramento Kings inside the raucous Intuit Dome crowd. Similar to their first meeting last season on Dec. 30, where the Clippers had their largest home margin of victory ever against the Kings, 131-90, the Clippers took command for nearly the entirety of the second half. Facing a Kings defense that held opponents to only a low mark of 98 points twice last season, the Clippers hit their stride from deep through the early stages, something Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue felt his team could accomplish. “We shot 52% from the field and 40% from three, those are some good numbers,” said Lue. “We just got to make sure we play the right way every possession, we have no margin for error.” Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Nico Alba - The Sporting Tribune Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Efficiency was not a factor for the Clippers coming into this season, as they ranked third in the league last year at a near 49% shooting clip from the floor and had a near 41% mark from beyond the arc in all games against the Kings last season. Rather, it was their volume of shots that ranked amongst the bottom 10 teams in the league, coming in second-to-last with 40.5 field goals made. item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) makes a deep three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES - The Los Angeles Clippers entered tonight’s regular-season opener with a lot of questions to be answered amid all the off-season turmoil and an injury list that piled on throughout the offseason. Yet, the Clippers answered the call tonight with a resounding 121-96 victory over the Sacramento Kings inside the raucous Intuit Dome crowd. Similar to their first meeting last season on Dec. 30, where the Clippers had their largest home margin of victory ever against the Kings, 131-90, the Clippers took command for nearly the entirety of the second half. Facing a Kings defense that held opponents to only a low mark of 98 points twice last season, the Clippers hit their stride from deep through the early stages, something Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue felt his team could accomplish. “We shot 52% from the field and 40% from three, those are some good numbers,” said Lue. “We just got to make sure we play the right way every possession, we have no margin for error.” Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Nico Alba - The Sporting Tribune Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Efficiency was not a factor for the Clippers coming into this season, as they ranked third in the league last year at a near 49% shooting clip from the floor and had a near 41% mark from beyond the arc in all games against the Kings last season. Rather, it was their volume of shots that ranked amongst the bottom 10 teams in the league, coming in second-to-last with 40.5 field goals made. There was no shortage of offense tonight as the Clippers rained down 41 points in the first quarter alone, much higher than their 17-point effort last time these two faced off in Sacramento back on Feb. 6. With already seven triples deposited by the start of the second quarter, the Clippers stretched their lead to 18 points and were clicking on both ends. However, the low point of the game ensued for the Clippers following an early Kings timeout, as they roared back with a 25-14 run to close out the half while the Clippers held on to a slim 61-54 lead after missing 13 of their 18 shots during that stretch. The Clippers played a much better brand of basketball in the second half, as they spaced the floor and created opportunities for their top threats. In a game that would potentially feature the No. 5 overall pick and Clippers’ rookie sensation Keaton Wagler, it was the veterans who provided that spark. Guard Darius Garland led all scorers with 30 points on 11-for-19 shooting. In arguably his first ever season as the leader and overall officiator, Garland led the charge and has racked up double figures in all 20 games as a Clipper. “Darius I thought coming out (set) the tone early, scoring the ball offensively,” said Lue. “Then in the second half getting everyone else involved, he did a really good job of orchestrating that second half.” In a new role as the backup Center, Brook Lopez controlled the low post and paint, recording a double-double with 17 points and 11 rebounds to begin his 18th season. Los Angeles Clippers center Brook Lopez (11) makes the turnaround mid range jumper during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Nico Alba - The Sporting Tribune Los Angeles Clippers center Brook Lopez (11) makes the turnaround mid range jumper during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. That back-court and front-court tandem helped ignite a massive run in the third quarter following a early Clippers timeout where the Kings trimmed it down to five. Nailing 8 of their next 13 shots in the quarter, the Clippers built their lead back up to 18 and then some, limiting the Kings to just 14 points the remaining of the quarter. The Kings were never able to trim it back into single digits the rest of the way after they were a down by a mere two-possessions. “As the second half started, I thought we did a better job of just moving the basketball, moving bodies, and making the right plays,” said Lue. “We’ve got to continue doing that every single night.” The Kings also saw contributions from their veteran stars in guard Zach LaVine and center Domantas Sabonis. Lavine dropped 28 points on 10-of-19 shooting from the floor, while the double-double machine in Sabonis put up another by the half, finishing with 14 points and 18 rebounds. Those 18 boards for Sabonis not only matched a season high from an injury-riddled year last season where he played in just 19 games, but it was also the most in a season opener for any player in Kings history. The biggest story of the night for the Kings was the royal-less debut from their No. 7 draft pick and point guard Darius Acuff Jr. While he got some good looks from the floor and attacked the rim, he shot a poor 5-for-24 from the floor and 0-for-7 from deep, finishing with 12 points. Wagler, on the other hand, got more reps in the second half with an already sizable lead. Wagler finished with 15 points and had 10 in the second half. He also collected five rebounds and five assists. In this bout of banged-up squads, the Clippers earned their 113th victory against the Kings and their 69th against them at home. With already the third best overall record in the league since the 2011-2012 season and the longest active winning-season streak of 15, the Clippers begin this 2026-27 campaign victorious. They will now take a short trip up north on Interstate 110 and take on their cross-city rivals the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday with new goals in mind. “I loved our activity, I loved our physicality,” said Lue. “We got to use our speed, we gotta be aggressive when teams attack the paint, we got to just scrap every single night (and) have each other’s backs.” Tip-off is set for 7:00 p.m.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard sounds off on Raptors’ historic season opener
item.description: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Kawhi Leonard sounds off on Raptors’ historic season opener appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kawhi Leonard is eager to move on from his controversial stint with the Los Angeles Clippers in his return to the Toronto Raptors . He is off to a good start. Leonard helped the Raptors blow out the Chicago Bulls, 135-92, at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday. He had 23 points, six rebounds, and four steals in 24 minutes. Their 43-point victory was the biggest season-opening win in team history. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Leonard touted their impressive performance on both ends, including leading by as much as 48 points. “You couldn’t ask for a better welcome-back game, you know. We won, we have a good team effort out there defensively, and got out on transition offensively,” said the two-time Finals MVP in the postgame interview. He acknowledged that he is still adjusting in his return to Toronto , which he led to its first title in 2019, but issued a strong message to the home crowd. “Just still getting acquainted with all my teammates, the offense, the defensive schemes. It’s the first game, so we gonna keep building and try and get better,” added Leonard. “Just thank everybody for coming out. We’re gonna try to make a special season. Hopefully, we can keep this rolling, and the best is yet to come.” Kawhi Leonard in his first postgame interview in his 2nd stint with the Toronto Raptors: “Just thank everybody for coming out. We’re gonna try to make a special season, hopefully.” “Hopefully we could keep this rolling, and the best is yet to come.” 🎥: Sportsnet 🎤:… pic.twitter.com/dknX480ONt — Omer Osman (@OmerOsman200) October 22, 2026 Immanuel Quickley had 23 points, four rebounds, seven assists, and two steals, while Scottie Barnes added 23 points, four rebounds, and three assists. The Raptors shot 45% from the field and scored 35 points off the Bulls’ 27 turnovers. The Clippers shipped Leonard to the Raptors in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, and five draft picks. Toronto will visit the Washington Wizards on Friday. Related: Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard shares clear message to those waiting for his peak form Related: Former Raptors star Serge Ibaka sends heartfelt message on Kawhi Leonard’s Toronto return

item.title: Maple Leafs Need to Have a Serious Talk about Easton Cowan
item.description: The Toronto Maple Leafs need to seriously talk about Easton Cowan's place on the team, given the start to his season. Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs cannot ignore the fact that Easton Cowan has become more than just a top prospect. The Cowboy’s start to this season has fully entrenched him as a member of the team’s top six. And that situation should lead to a serious conversation about Cowan’s place in the lineup. At the moment, Cowan has a firm grasp on a top-six lineup spot with John Tavares out with an injury. But when Tavares returns, the team needs to keep Cowan in the top six. There’s really no question about it. Cowan has looked increasingly confident playing on a line with Nick Paul and Kirill Marchenko. If anything, his goal against Columbus on Tuesday night exemplified just how far Cowan has come. EASTON COWAN WITH THE SHORTY!!! 🤠 pic.twitter.com/CGgKr9067p — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 21, 2026 With the Maple Leafs up 3-1 midway through the second period, Easton Cowan was on the penalty kill with William Nylander. The duo set off on a rush, leading to Cowan’s first career shorthanded goal. That goal exemplified two things about Cowan this season. The first thing is that the organization wants to find more playing time for the 21-year-old. And the only real place where the team could find more ice time in on the penalty kill. Cowan rewarded the Maple Leafs’ belief in him by netting the shortie. The other thing is that Easton Cowan has earned the coaching staff’s trust. He’s no longer the type of player that only goes out there in a sheltered role. He’s become the sort of player that coaches can deploy in any situation. And, at the end of the day, that makes him highly valuable to the organization. Easton Cowan Is No Longer Part of Trade Talk One of the rumors that’s out there is the fact that Cowan is no longer part of trade discussions . Two seasons ago, the Maple Leafs dangled both Cowan and Fraser Minten in front of the Carolina Hurricanes in a potential Mikko Rantanen trade. The Hurricanes had reportedly accepted one of them in the potential deal, before eventually backing out. While everyone knows how well Minten has turned out with the Boston Bruins, it’s horrifying to think what would have happened if Easton Cowan, for example, had landed in Carolina. While missing out on Rantanen really stung at the time, it’s good to know that the Maple Leafs managed to hold on to one solid prospect. Maple Leafs May End up with the Steal of First-Round in 2023 Draft All told, the Maple Leafs may end up with the biggest steal of the first round in the 2023 NHL Draft. Toronto picked Easton Cowan 28 th overall, after some rather doubtful picks. It’s worth bearing in mind that this is the draft in which Connor Bedard went first overall, Leo Carlsson second, and Adam Fantilli third. And when looking at the trajectory of these players, Cowan isn’t far behind. No, The Cowboy isn’t on track to become captain. He isn’t likely to get the massive payday

An official was just right behind Ball when he made the journey, but the traveling was not called. Even ESPN announcers Mike Breen, Tim Legler and Richard Jefferson were baffled by the non-call live on air. Lonzo Ball Calls Out LaMelo Ball Getty LaMelo Ball #1 of the Minnesota Timberwolves reacts during the third quarter of a preseason game against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on October 12, 2026 in New York City. In a post on X , formerly known as Twitter, Lonzo Ball trolled his youngest brother by calling him out for the viral play. “Travel lmaoooo,” Lonzo tweeted. Travel lmaoooo — Lonzo Ball (@ZO2_) October 22, 2026 Lonzo, who remains a free agent, is at a crossroads in his NBA career. There are rumors that he might retire, but there’s no official announcement from the former No. 2 pick. Here are some of the reactions to LaMelo’s “journey” that wasn’t called: @LasVegasNBAteam : “Ref needs to be fired wtf was that” @SoFLFella : “And this is why the viewership is dropping. The hell is that?” @edgarwoo : “He traveled back to Minnesota.” @MiilitantMidget : “Somebody will try to convince you that’s a gather step. The NBA is a joke.” Getty LaMelo Ball #1 of the Minnesota Timberwolves celebrates his three-point basket against the Detroit Pistons in the first quarter during a preseason game at Target Center on October 14, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. @Bored_Certified : “Fun Fact: The last time an NBA ref called a traveling violation was 1998.” @BadSportsRefs : “Some idiot will come out defending this, just wait” @NostraTomas : “Just remove traveling from game and make dribbling optional” @Goducks2003 : “Night 2 and the traveling is worse than last season. It’s literally like going to one of those 4th grade kids basketball games where they let them travel and double dribble. This is how bad this looks @nba” Anthony Edwards Leads Timberwolves to Win vs. Heat Getty Anthony Edwards #5 of the Minnesota Timberwolves reacts against the Miami Heat during the second half at Kaseya Center on October 21, 2026 in Miami, Florida. While LaMelo Ball went viral for the wrong reasons, Anthony Edwards took over in the Minnesota Timberwolves’ win against the Miami Heat. Edwards exploded for 45 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and two steals on 16-for-29 shooting from the field, including nine 3-pointers made. Jaden McDaniels added 17 points and eight rebounds, while Jonathan Kuminga scored 12 points in his Timberwolves debut. Rudy Gobert only had five points but grabbed 15 rebounds. On the other hand, Giannis Antetokounmpo dropped 35 points and six rebounds in his first game for the Heat. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Lonzo Ball Reacts to LaMelo Ball’s Viral Travel Non-Call in Timberwolves Debut appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Hornets' Offseason Acquisitions Play Key Role in Opening Night Win
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets started off the 2026-27 season with a 110-103 win over the Brooklyn Nets . The Hornets were active in the offseason, retooling their roster around Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel by adding a mix of young talent and veterans. Some of their new acquisitions played a major role in their opening night win over the Nets. Naz Reid, the centerpiece of the return from the LaMelo Ball trade, had a great performance, finishing with 20 points, 11 rebounds, and seven assists, shooting 8-for-19 from the field and 4-for-10 from three. Reid was a sixth man with the Minnesota Timberwolves , but proved he could be a valuable starter in his first game in Charlotte. Veteran guard Dennis Schroder got the start in his Hornets debut, as Coby White was out with a left calf strain. Schroder played 35 minutes, finishing with 19 points, four rebounds, and six assists while shooting 7-for-13 from the floor. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That wasn't all for the new acquisitions, as Grayson Allen provided a spark off the bench, averaging 21 points, three rebounds, and four assists, shooting 6-for-9 from the field and 5-for-8 from behind the arc. Allen's shooting was pivotal for the Hornets, and he could be a great fit for Charles Lee's system. Royce O'Neale was also solid off the bench, with eight points, four rebounds, a steal, and a block, shooting 3-for-6 from the floor and 2-for-5 from distance. The Hornets were without Knueppel, one of their best players, but still came away with a win. Knueppel finished second in Rookie of the Year voting in the 2025-26 season, averaging 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, shooting 47.5 percent from the field and 42.5 percent from downtown. When Knueppel returns to the lineup, Charlotte's offense could reach the next level. Miller was the leader for the Hornets in shot attempts, as he had 18 points, shooting 7-for-21 from the floor and 3-for-14 from three. It wasn't an efficient game from Miller, but he should have a great 2026-27 season after signing a five-year, $209 million extension with the franchise. Starting center Moussa Diabate stood out for Charlotte, as he had 17 points, eight rebounds, three assists, and five steals while shooting 7-for-11 from the field. It's a strong start to the season for the Hornets, as they look to make it into the playoffs for the first time since the 2015-16 season.

item.title: Florentino Perez to miss Barcelona vs Real Madrid El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou
item.description: Florentino Perez to miss Barcelona vs Real Madrid El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou Real Madrid president Florentino Perez will not attend Sunday’s El Clasico against Barcelona at Spotify Camp Nou, according to Mundo Deportivo , with the decision also ruling out the traditional pre-match lunch between the clubs’ directors. His absence comes amid strained institutional relations between the Spanish giants, ensuring there will be no meeting with Barcelona president Joan Laporta before kick-off. The fixture is already attracting attention for Jose Mourinho’s return to Barcelona, but the lack of a presidential reunion adds more controversy to a rivalry that has increasingly extended beyond the pitch. Florentino Perez absence means no directors’ lunch Perez will not travel to Barcelona for the latest meeting between the clubs, continuing a pattern of absences from Camp Nou in recent seasons. According to the report, the usual gathering between the two boards will not take place either, removing a long-standing part of the pre-match protocol surrounding El Clasico. Florentino Perez will not attend this season’s El Clasico at Camp Nou. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The relationship between Barcelona and Real Madrid has deteriorated since Real Madrid began pursuing the Negreira case publicly. The dispute has contributed to a breakdown in institutional relations, making the absence of both Perez and the traditional directors’ luncheon more than a routine scheduling detail. Real Madrid will still have a presence in the VIP area, although the representation is expected to be more limited than in previous editions. At last season’s corresponding Clasico at Camp Nou, Pirri, Real Madrid’s honorary president, was the only representative from the Madrid club in the VIP box. This time, a Real Madrid vice-president is expected to attend. Tyler, the Creator among expected El Clasico guests Barcelona no longer have any relationship with Real Madrid. (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO/AFP via Getty Images) Attention will also extend beyond the club executives, with the list of VIPs and dignitaries still awaiting final confirmation. Tyler, The Creator is expected to be among those attending. The artist’s logo, alongside his GOLF brand, will feature on the front of Barcelona’s shirt for the occasion. His anticipated presence offers a different kind of spotlight for the fixture, which combines sporting rivalry, commercial visibility and institutional tension. Yet the most consequential absence may be Perez’s.

item.title: “Help the team as best I can”
item.description: “Help the team as best I can” Raphael Onyedika talks about his first home win as an Eagle, previous experience of Dortmund and his physical stamina. Raphael, congratulations on the first home win. How did it feel to stand in front of the fans with three points for the first time? “Thanks! There were great emotions. Regardless of the feelings it triggered in me, it was first and foremost important to have picked up three points against Köln – for us as a team just as much as for the fans.” You’re the only player who’s completed 690 of a possible 690 competitive minutes this season. Where does that endurance come from? “I’m in top shape and want to help the team as best I can. The team’s success is the priority. The more I can contribute to that, the better. In general, we all do a lot of training on the physical aspect because that’s the basis for how we play. It certainly helps me that I’ve been used to playing two matches a week in the last four or five years.” Who is your idol? “Ronaldinho was one of my heroes when I was younger. In terms of playing style, I try to take some things from Paul Pogba in his best years. But he also had a slightly different profile as a midfielder to me.” You’ve mostly played alongside Mario Götze and Noel Aseko so far. Does your game change depending on which of them is next to you, or do all the tasks remain the same? “The guys next to me are different players in some ways, but that doesn’t change anything for me. I’m the most defensive of our midfielders. In any case, the coach wants us to develop a connection with every single teammate. I take that on board and enjoy playing with Mario, Noel or also Oscar Højlund.” You returned from international duty early. Why was that? “The idea came from the club, so that we had more time together to prepare at the end of the international period. After getting the okay from the Nigeria Football Federation, I came back early.” Do you remember your first match against Dortmund? “Very well, actually. First matchday in the Champions League two years ago with Club Brugge. We held our own really well for a long time and had chances to lead 1-0 or even 2-0. The game flipped in the final 20 minutes, BVB scored three goals in the final quarter of an hour and won 3-0. It was strange: the feeling that we held our own well and yet deserved to lose by that margin.” You go to Dortmund on Saturday, in front of around 80,000 people. Have you ever played in a comparable stadium? “I can’t recall playing in front of such a big crowd. I’ve heard a lot about the stadium, the atmosphere and not least the opposition team. I think it’s going to be nice and challenging. We are doing everything we can to be perfectly prepared, mentally as well. It’s vital to remember that there is always room for improvement, even after a win like the one against Cologne. We are a good side, but we have to make sure we get the details right over the full 90 to 95 minutes of every single game!”

item.title: Vinicius sinking, Camavinga’s rise | Three takeaways from Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig
item.description: Vinicius sinking, Camavinga’s rise | Three takeaways from Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig For the second straight game, Real Madrid racked up a 4-1 win last night against RB Leipzig, and it is safe to say that the result was thoroughly deserved. There were moments of panic in the game from which Thibaut Courtois was forced to make extra-terrestrial saves to keep his side alive. Once they took the lead, however, Real Madrid inflicted serial damage on the visitors and found themselves 3-0 up by the 83rd minute. The visitors then pulled one back, but Yan Diomande delivered the final blow with a wonderful strike. Madrid Universal brings you three takeaways from Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig . Vinicius’ future looks bleak Being suspended in La Liga for four games, Vinicius Jr.’s only chance of playing football now comes in the UEFA Champions League. Jose Mourinho thus decided to hand the player a start last night, hoping he would redeem himself. Vinicius Jr. was not at his best against RB Leipzig. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) While Vinicius was slightly better than he had looked in recent games, he was again outperformed and overshadowed, even though he replaced him for only the final 20 minutes. In 70 minutes on the field, the Brazilian star failed to rack up a single key pass or accurate cross. He did have two shots on target, but neither really looked like a scoring position. What is more appalling is that the Brazilian star did not complete a single dribble in 70 minutes – something that is very unlike him and a clear indication that he is slowly but surely sinking under pressure. Coming on to replace him, meanwhile, Diomande scored a stunning goal, racked up one key pass and looked like a regular threat down the left flank for Real Madrid. The difference between him and Vinicius was clear as day. Given how matters are progressing, Vinicius appears to be slowly reconciling to the fact that he is losing his spot in the side and that there is nothing he can do about it. His decline is unfortunate and difficult to watch, but Diomande appears to be growing into a deserved starter on the left wing. Camavinga’s big statement Camavinga started alongside Bernardo Silva against RB Leipzig. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Jose Mourinho completely changed the look of Real Madrid’s midfield last night, bringing on Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into the lineup as the double pivot. Both players have not had a lot of minutes in recent weeks – particularly the Frenchman who only saw fringe minutes after the international break despite doing well for Zinedine Zidane and France. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) While Vinicius was slightly better than he had looked in recent games, he was again outperformed and overshadowed, even though he replaced him for only the final 20 minutes. In 70 minutes on the field, the Brazilian star failed to rack up a single key pass or accurate cross. He did have two shots on target, but neither really looked like a scoring position. Coming on to replace him, meanwhile, Diomande scored a stunning goal, racked up one key pass and looked like a regular threat down the left flank for Real Madrid. The difference between him and Vinicius was clear as day. Given how matters are progressing, Vinicius appears to be slowly reconciling to the fact that he is losing his spot in the side and that there is nothing he can do about it. His decline is unfortunate and difficult to watch, but Diomande appears to be growing into a deserved starter on the left wing. Camavinga’s big statement Camavinga started alongside Bernardo Silva against RB Leipzig. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Jose Mourinho completely changed the look of Real Madrid’s midfield last night, bringing on Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into the lineup as the double pivot. Both players have not had a lot of minutes in recent weeks – particularly the Frenchman who only saw fringe minutes after the international break despite doing well for Zinedine Zidane and France. After a long time, Camavinga played all 90 minutes for Los Blancos and he dropped a performance that once again showed the world why he was so highly rated at one point. He may not have finished with a goal or an assist, but the control he provided in midfield was far superior to what Aurelien Tchouameni usually offers. In 90 minutes, Camavinga completed 92% of his passes, 67% of long balls and completed 100% of the three dribbles he attempted. Defensively, he stood out with six recoveries, an interception, three tackles won and a staggering 14 duels won. For Camavinga to come back into such good form, needless to say, comes as massive news for Real Madrid and Jose Mourinho. Moreover, his positive partnership with Bernardo Silva hands the manager a new rotational option in midfield. Momentum when it’s needed most The wind is fresh in Real Madrid’s sails, and for the first time this season, Mourinho’s men seem to be treading a path with a clear plan and good confidence. Real Madrid now have the momentum. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) The timing of such a purple patch, in that sense, could not have been any better. Having scored eight goals and conceded just two in their last two games, Real Madrid will now believe in their chances against Barcelona at the weekend. For a long time, the Catalans were seen as overwhelming favourites against Real Madrid, especially because of Los Blancos’ midfield situation. With order now restored and some semblance of stability in the department, Real Madrid also have a good chance of capitalising on the Clasico. The importance of the momentum the team currently possesses, in that sense, cannot be understated and all eyes now shift to the weekend’s game against Barcelona which is massive for the title race. A win, and Real Madrid are back within three points and well within reach of the lead in La Liga. A defeat, however, will put them nine points behind Barcelona and in a position of great weakness in the domestic competition.

item.title: Chargers in trouble over Travis Kelce incident as major NFL punishment looms
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley could face a significant NFL fine after his controversial tackle on Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce during their 22-6 defeat. The incident has attracted attention after Kelce appeared to tweak his ankle during the play. The veteran tight end briefly left the game before returning, easing concerns among Chiefs supporters. However, the tackle has continued to generate debate, with questions being raised over whether Henley used an illegal hip-drop technique. Daiyan Henley could face NFL fine for Travis Kelce tackle Clips of the tackle have circulated online, with Chiefs fans and analysts questioning the legality of Henley’s challenge. The NFL prohibits hip-drop tackles because of the injury risk involved. The banned technique involves a defender unweighting their body, swivelling their hips and dropping onto a ball carrier’s legs to bring them down. The play involving Kelce has prompted scrutiny over whether Henley’s tackle met those criteria. However, the league has not officially confirmed that it is investigating the incident or announced any disciplinary action. If the NFL determines that Henley committed an illegal hip-drop tackle, he could face a five-figure penalty. According to the league’s official website, the baseline fine for a first offence is $17,911, rising to $23,882 for repeat violations. Those figures mean the Chargers linebacker could face a costly consequence if the league rules against him. However, any potential punishment remains unconfirmed. Kelce’s brief absence from the game also raised concerns for Kansas City, given his importance to the Chiefs’ offence. He was able to return, while head coach Andy Reid offered a reassuring update after the victory. Reid indicated that Kelce might be sore but said he would “be ok”. The Chiefs will now hope their tight end avoids any lingering problems as they continue their unbeaten start to the season. Meanwhile, the Chargers remain winless after six games, adding to the pressure following another defeat. Henley’s situation will depend on the NFL’s review and whether the league determines that the tackle breached its rules. Until an official decision is announced, a fine remains a possibility rather than a confirmed punishment. item.title: JD Vance Meets His Favorite NFL Team, but Most Players Walk Past
item.description: Photo by Kenny Holston-Pool/Getty Images Vice President JD Vance visited his favorite NFL team, but the players’ reaction wasn’t what he expected. A new video captured the awkward moment Bengals players walked right past the VP after practice. How Cincinnati Bengals players interacted with the vice president Cincinnati Bengals players gave Vice President JD Vance a notably cold reception during his surprise visit to Paycor Stadium, according to NBC 5 Cincinnati. The Ohio native stopped by after speaking at a rally in the Cincinnati suburb of Sharonville on Wednesday. Most players offered little more than a passing nod as they walked past him toward the locker room after practice. JD Vance greets Bengals players on the way out pic.twitter.com/lMKvYRpMfE — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 Sports Director Charlie Clifford’s 18-second video captured tight end Drew Sample fist-bumping Vance’s son Vivek before briefly shaking the vice president’s hand. Sample appeared to be the only player in the clip who shook Vance’s hand. Clifford later explained on air that Vance was spending time with the players as practice ended. Head coach Zac Taylor did shake Vance’s hand before heading into the locker room. A separate video from Cincinnati Enquirer reporter Kelsey Conway captured that interaction. Star quarterback Joe Burrow told reporters he did not get a chance to meet with Vance. “He, uhh, came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn’t get to,” Burrow said. The 29-year-old added he only learned about the visit after practice had already started. Burrow deflected a question about his reaction to the visit by turning the focus to himself. “A lot of people around. You know, that’s what I love about what I do is, it brings a lot of people together, and people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, watch what I do, and watch all the work that I’ve put in, to come and watch greatness,” Burrow said. Vance grew up in Middletown, roughly a 45-minute drive from downtown Cincinnati. The 3-2 Bengals will face the 4-2 Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday. The post JD Vance Meets His Favorite NFL Team, but Most Players Walk Past appeared first on Reality Tea .
item.content:encoded: Photo by Kenny Holston-Pool/Getty Images Vice President JD Vance visited his favorite NFL team, but the players’ reaction wasn’t what he expected. A new video captured the awkward moment Bengals players walked right past the VP after practice. How Cincinnati Bengals players interacted with the vice president Cincinnati Bengals players gave Vice President JD Vance a notably cold reception during his surprise visit to Paycor Stadium, according to NBC 5 Cincinnati. The Ohio native stopped by after speaking at a rally in the Cincinnati suburb of Sharonville on Wednesday. Most players offered little more than a passing nod as they walked past him toward the locker room after practice. JD Vance greets Bengals players on the way out pic.twitter.com/lMKvYRpMfE — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 Sports Director Charlie Clifford’s 18-second video captured tight end Drew Sample fist-bumping Vance’s son Vivek before briefly shaking the vice president’s hand. Sample appeared to be the only player in the clip who shook Vance’s hand. Clifford later explained on air that Vance was spending time with the players as practice ended. Head coach Zac Taylor did shake Vance’s hand before heading into the locker room. A separate video from Cincinnati Enquirer reporter Kelsey Conway captured that interaction. Star quarterback Joe Burrow told reporters he did not get a chance to meet with Vance. “He, uhh, came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn’t get to,” Burrow said. The 29-year-old added he only learned about the visit after practice had already started. Burrow deflected a question about his reaction to the visit by turning the focus to himself. “A lot of people around. You know, that’s what I love about what I do is, it brings a lot of people together, and people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, watch what I do, and watch all the work that I’ve put in, to come and watch greatness,” Burrow said. Vance grew up in Middletown, roughly a 45-minute drive from downtown Cincinnati. The 3-2 Bengals will face the 4-2 Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday. item.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg ‘lost all respect’ for Luka Doncic
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Matched up with Luka Doncic, Yaxel Lendeborg, the Warriors’ bold and brash rookie, came away with at least one lesson from his NBA debut. “Being in there firsthand, just watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect, man,” Lendeborg said after Golden State’s 127-105 season-opening loss to the Lakers . “That was awful.” The most entertaining part of a blowout loss for the Warriors was undoubtedly Lendeborg’s ongoing back-and-forth with the Lakers’ equally loud-mouthed superstar . Lendeborg finished with 12 points, four personal fouls and one technical in 29 minutes. Yaxel Lendeborg defends Luka Doncic during the Warriors’ 127-105 loss to the Lakers on Oct. 21, 2026 in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images He often drew the defensive matchup with Doncic, who went off for a game-high 28 with nine free throws. But Lendeborg’s biggest takeaway was all Doncic’s extracurriculars that came after the whistle. “Like, me getting frustrated, it’s not about the foul getting called. It’s about him complaining the entire game,” Lendeborg said. “Then you get the foul called — congratulations, bro — and you talk to me like you did something great? That’s just weak. It kind of threw me off for a while. Because like I said, I had so much respect for him. Gone, man.” Though Doncic only made it to the line nine times, Lendeborg said it felt like 30. Doncic mostly only ran his mouth on the court, merely saying afterward that the No. 11 overall pick was “talking like crazy.” Lendeborg, on the other hand, was happy to get into the nitty gritty. “I said a couple cuss words,” Lendeborg said. “That’s why I got the technical. But I was letting him know, because he was laughing and talking all this because of one foul call.” Lendeborg bit on one of Doncic’s pump fakes midway through the first half, and the two were off and running — their mouths, anyway. Doncic pointed and laughed. Lendeborg responded. At one point, Lendeborg started putting both his hands behind his back when guarding Doncic. Yaxel Lendeborg (left) and Luka Doncic look on during a break in the action in the Warriors’ loss to the Lakers. NBAE via Getty Images “I tried my best,” he said. “I still got called.” The back-and-forth continued for the remainder of the first half, hitting an inflection point after Lendeborg successfully defended Doncic on a step-back 3. He followed him back down the court, yapping all the way, until he was T’d up for the first time in his career. Doncic returned the favor after banking in a half-court shot at the buzzer going into halftime. Coach Steve Kerr said it was “kind of ridiculous” that Lendeborg was the only one to draw a technical in the exchange. But he didn’t have a problem with his rookie’s confidence. Yaxel Lendeborg looks on during the Warriors’ loss to the Lakers. NBAE via Getty Images “They were jawing at each other. I think it was the words Yaxel chose that got him the T,” Kerr said, acknowledging that Doncic “kind of lured him in.” Lendeb

NBAE via Getty Images “I tried my best,” he said. “I still got called.” The back-and-forth continued for the remainder of the first half, hitting an inflection point after Lendeborg successfully defended Doncic on a step-back 3. I definitely thought that he was gonna do more than that.” If we learned anything from Lendeborg’s NBA debut, he may be the league’s most captivating newcomer, possibly even a spiritual successor to Draymond Green. A lot of flopping, a lot of foul baiting, a lot of praying to the ref,” Lendeborg said. “Interesting first game, for sure.”

item.title: Mets predicted to sign rival Phillies' $10.2M high-contact All-Star to replace Jorge Polanco
item.description: Mets predicted to sign rival Phillies' $10.2M high-contact All-Star to replace Jorge Polanco originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies could have a new-look roster next season as they try to figure out how to get back to the World Series. Their season ended at the hands of the Atlanta Braves in the Wild Card round, which likely isn't how they wanted to go out. The Phillies will now turn their attention to the offseason, and it remains unclear what comes next for All-Star Alec Bohm. “Even though it was a dreadful start to the season, it was good to see Bohm bounce back as the season progressed. Overall, .249/.315/.383 with 15 home runs and 88 RBI. The numbers certainly improved for the slugger, and he should be seen as a desirable target in free agency. However, whether or not he will be back with the Phillies remains to be seen. This is a team that is trying to get a little bit younger, and handing out another potential long-term deal to a veteran might not be what they want to do,” SI’s Nick Ziegler wrote. There is considerable uncertainty surrounding Bohm's future in Philadelphia. Based on the latest speculation, it appears increasingly possible that he will not return. “It doesn’t sound like Alec Bohm is especially likely to return to the Phillies,” Bleacher Report’s Tim Kelly wrote. Bohm should have several options in free agency, as he is a consistent contact hitter. MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand believes Bohm could join the New York Mets and take over at first base. “The Mets’ production at first base (.667 OPS) was third worst in the Majors, but Jorge Polanco is signed for $20 million next season. Their .684 OPS at third base ranked 19th in the Majors, but with Bo Bichette signed for $42 million in 2027 (with another $42 million player option for ‘28), the hot corner wouldn’t appear to be available. Owner Steve Cohen could look past the money owed to Polanco if he believes Bohm is a good fit for the Mets, who are coming off of two straight seasons without reaching the postseason,” Feinsand wrote. It is safe to say that the Jorge Polanco experiment hasn't gone according to plan for the Mets. They could use him as a designated hitter or at second base, potentially opening up another spot for Bohm. Bohm still has plenty of upside and could give New York another option in its lineup. Bohm played on a $10.2 million contract with the Phillies. The Mets could look to poach a player from one of their division rivals as they try to improve their roster. New York will be looking to have a better season, and adding Bohm could help the team accomplish that goal. item.title: Man Utd dressing room DRAMA! Michael Carrick fires back at Bruno Fernandes in public war of words after Red Devils humiliated by Como in Champions League horror show
item.description: Michael Carrick Bruno Fernandes Manchester United Como - Getty Images Manchester United’s season hit a new low on Wednesday night as a disastrous 4-1 defeat to Como sparked a public war of words between Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes. The humiliating Champions League result has left the manager’s future in serious doubt after a performance that lacked both tactical discipline and physical effort. Nightmare in northern Italy The Red Devils endured a miserable evening at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium, crashing to their fifth defeat in just 11 matches this term. Wednesday's dismal European outing also stretched their current winless streak to seven games across all competitions. The United skipper was withdrawn after 67 minutes on a night where the Premier League giants were completely outclassed. The aftermath quickly descended into chaos as captain and manager took bitter public swipes at each other over the root cause of the Italian collapse. Tactics versus effort debate Following his substitution, Fernandes pointed the finger directly at the dugout. The Portuguese playmaker questioned the game plan , stating: "It was a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind." When informed of those remarks during his post-match media duties, the 45-year-old manager refused to take the criticism lying down. Instead, Carrick fired back by openly questioning the basic work rate of his dressing room. "We actually were half-pressed man-to-man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that," Carrick explained. He then delivered a pointed message to Fernandes: "And whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." Como 1907 v Manchester United - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 Mounting pressure and fan apologies The messy public feud heavily intensifies the spotlight on the United boss. Having earned a new two-year deal in May following a third-place league finish, this sudden domestic and continental slump has firmly jeopardised his position. After apologising directly to the travelling support at the final whistle, the head coach was pressed on whether he feared the sack. He insisted his focus remained entirely on the club's frustrated fanbase rather than his own employment status. "Listen, I've not given my own position any thought. This is for the supporters; I was one of them watching that, and I wasn't happy at all," Carrick revealed. "I'm really angry, to be honest. We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight wasn't acceptable. I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure." item.title: Padres predicted to sign Yankees' $10M high-energy Silver Slugger to pair with Fernando Tatis
item.description: Padres predicted to sign Yankees' $10M high-energy Silver Slugger to pair with Fernando Tatis originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This is going to be a big offseason for Jazz Chisholm as he faces decisions about his future in free agency. The New York Yankees second baseman was left out of the starting lineup for some playoff games, which could have hurt his relationship with the team. This winter, or whenever the lockout ends, Chisholm will have the opportunity to choose where he wants to play. However, he has made it clear that he wants to stay in New York. “Chisholm, an All-Star for the second time in 2025, endured a down year at the plate and struggled both offensively and defensively in four appearances in the playoffs. Manager Aaron Boone left Chisholm out of the Yankees' starting lineup for two postseason games, including their season-ending loss on Wednesday. The fans at Yankee Stadium booed Chisholm after he fouled out to first base as a pinch hitter in the bottom of the seventh inning. Nevertheless, Chisholm would rather continue his career with the Yankees than exit in free agency," MLB Trade Rumors' wrote. If Chisholm decides not to return to New York, Bleacher Report's Zachary D. Rymer believes he should sign with the San Diego Padres . “Starting pitching will need to be a priority, but another bat should also be a must. The Padres specifically need more left-handed thump after getting just a .385 SLG from that side of the plate. They could also use more offensive production at second base, where Jake Cronenworth struggled in 2026. Also, does anyone else get the sense that San Diego would be a good spot for Chisholm's energy? He plays with a chip on his shoulder, and that's been the Padres' whole vibe as they have fought the Los Angeles Dodgers for control of the NL West throughout the 2020,” Rymer wrote. A move to San Diego could be an exciting opportunity for Chisholm, who would bring the kind of energy that fits with the rest of the organization. Seeing Chisholm and Fernando Tatis Jr. on the same team would be an intriguing possibility. Chisholm played on a $10 million contract with the Yankees last season. He also won a Silver Slugger not too long ago, adding to his appeal as a potential addition. San Diego could be an ideal fit for Chisholm and his energetic style of play. item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: How Brazil’s election result could shape women’s football in the country

It had been an incredible final but after the game the goalkeeper Carlinha used an interview to appeal to her fans: “Never again Bolsonaro in power,” she shouted to a record-breaking TV audience of 23 million people. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Sarina Wiegman signs contract extension to stay as England women head coach until 2029
item.description: Wiegman says she ‘cannot think of a better job in football’ She can target three European titles in row with Lionesses Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract to continue as the head coach of England women for Euro 2029. Her deal was due to expire after the World Cup next summer and this extension gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row. Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021 , also led her native Netherlands side to European Championship glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Florian Wirtz takes on more responsibility in Liverpool’s attack while Pierre Sage is under pressure at Crystal Palace Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s physicality overpowering Bryan Mbeumo in Manchester United’s area at a corner grabbed him a fifth goal in 10 outings for Leeds: a pretty respectable ratio. “I just tried to cause a ruckus,” said Leeds’ No 9. “I make it difficult for the defender. I read the flight of the ball and was quickest to react. I feel really comfortable [here]. I feel the support from the club and the fans and it is a great feeling stepping on to the pitch, particularly at Elland Road.” Of the contenders to be understudy to Harry Kane as England’s centre-forward, Calvert-Lewin may be the lead act – if he can stay injury-free, which has been a difficulty throughout his career. item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...
